topSignals.title: SK Eternix starts commercial operation of three Bloom Energy SOFC power plants (Icheon + Paju, South Korea) explicitly citing AI data center and semiconductor-cluster demand near Seoul.
topSignals.text: Icheon (8.9 MW) and Paju Unit 1 (9.9 MW) began operating Oct 19; Paju Unit 2 (9.2 MW) follows next month, bringing the three-site total to 28 MW (~222 GWh/yr projected) on a combined ₩159.4B investment. SK Eternix plans to pair the fleet with solar, wind and storage and offer PPA/VPP services. This is a new named Bloom Energy SOFC customer/operator (distinct from SK ecoplant) and the first dedicated AIDC-linked deployment logged in South Korea. MoneyToday (KR)

items.text: Elcogen (priority): No new News-category item since Sept 21 (Metrosert cooperation), confirmed by direct fetch today — 33 days quiet. Status unchanged: elcoStack E3000 G2 platform (75% FC electrical efficiency / 90% with heat recovery, 33 kWh/kg H2 SOEC — vendor claims) in volume production at the 360 MW/yr ELCO I Tallinn factory.

Topsoe (priority): No new solid-oxide-specific release since Aug 27 (H1 2026 results/SOEC pathway reset), confirmed by direct fetch today — 58 days quiet; topsoe.com/press-releases remains dominated by SAF/ammonia/e-methanol contract news, out of SOFC/SOEC scope.
Today's dedicated rotation — new Tier 3 cycle, round 1 (Reverion, Convion, Hexis, Doosan Fuel Cell, SK ecoplant, Weichai), 7-day lookback:
Reverion: Results were the already-logged Sept 18 Doosan $78M/€72M SOFC stack supply contract and Sept 29 $175M/€150M Series B — no new 2026 item.
Convion: Results were the standing HD Hyundai (HD Hyundai/HD Hydrogen) acquisition history (2024) and a Wärtsilä fuel-cell-business divestiture background piece — no new dated item.
Hexis: Results were legacy ownership-history coverage (h2e Power/Viessmann) — no new 2026 item.

Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: A Sept 15 Herald Corp article on an additional 322.2B-won ($240M) PAFC supply contract with its "Hyaxxium" US subsidiary (bringing cumulative contracts to 823.6B won) resurfaced — confirmed pre-dated (Sept 15) and PAFC-based, not SOFC; not adopted as new.

SK ecoplant: Results were the already-logged 2023-vintage SK ecoplant/GDS Singapore SOFC story. A related but distinct entity, SK Eternix, is covered separately under Top Signal #1 / AI Data Center Deployments — it is a Bloom Energy customer/operator, not a stack maker, so it does not change this line.
Weichai: No new item; the July 30 Southeast Asia microgrid release and the standing Ceres-Weichai SOFC licensing deal are unchanged.
Sweep 1 — "Reverion OR Convion OR Hexis OR Doosan Fuel Cell OR SK ecoplant": No new item beyond the above.

Sweep 2 — "Watt Fuel Cell OR OxEon Energy OR Nexceris OR Kawasaki Heavy Industries OR Miura": No new item; results were the standing Miura/Ceres 4.2kW CHP Japan launch and legacy Nexceris LEVER-process coverage.

Tier 2 sweep — "Bloom Energy OR FuelCell Energy OR Ceres Power OR Sunfire OR SolydEra": No new item; results were SEO-aggregator (enkiai.com) recaps of already-logged deals, the Sept 2 FuelCell Energy Q3 FY2026 release (75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, already on file), Sunfire's standing Schwarzheide SOEC test-facility construction, and SolydEra's standing PMX platform/Dynelectro MoU. No Tier 2 company had a genuinely new item today.
Competitor roster: SOFC systems for data centers

Bloom Energy: Deployed/signed at multiple named sites — Oracle/Project Jupiter (NM), AEP (1 GW), Brookfield EaaS, Nebius (328 MW, Finland), Equinix (>100 MW/19 sites), Aligned "Project Phoenix" (2 GW, PA), Hitachi (Japan), and now SK Eternix (Icheon/Paju, Korea, 28 MW, operational).

FuelCell Energy (incl. HyAxiom-branded products): Signed orders/PPAs — Fit Energy (up to 380 MW), Inuverse Korea (up to 100 MW), 75 MW Texas Capacity Reservation Agreement, SDCL (up to 450 MW). No named deployment live yet.

Doosan Fuel Cell/HyAxiom: Signed order — US AI data center supply contract (KRW 823.6B cumulative with Hyaxxium, mixed SOFC/PAFC); separately supplies SOFC stacks to Reverion. No named data-center site of its own yet.
Convion: Pipeline-only/pre-commercial under HD Hyundai ownership; no named data-center customer.
SK ecoplant: Pipeline-only (2023-vintage GDS Singapore SOFC deal); no new named data-center deployment.
Ceres Power's SOFC licensees (Doosan, Delta Electronics, Weichai): Licensing/pipeline-only; no named data-center deployment via Ceres licensing directly.
Reverion: Pipeline-only — Doosan-supplied SOFC stacks for rSOC power plants (Germany); no named data-center customer yet.
Petra Power: Pre-commercial, no named customer; first infrastructure deployment targeted 2028.

lcoe.text: Carry-forward, unchanged:* Virginia data-center electricity tax ($0.011/kWh); PJM Reliability Backstop ceiling (~$202.6/kW-year avoided-cost benchmark, filing suspended pending Feb 28, 2027 paper hearing); FCEL Torrington capex ($200–275M for 350–500 MW/yr by 2028); AEP/Bloom bundled utility-purchase benchmark ($2,944/kW capital+service); Germany's Netzpaket redispatch-curtailment risk (18–20% uncompensated annual-output exposure) for non-islanded SOFC deployments.

Pending calendar (updated):* German Netzpaket/EEG 2027 Bundestag vote targeted for the week of Nov 9–13 (2.5 weeks out), Bundesrat Nov 20; German KWK-Gesetz cabinet consideration remains undated past its Oct 14 target; FCEL lead-plaintiff deadline Nov 10 (17 days); PJM backstop paper hearing runs to Feb 28, 2027; next EIA STEO Nov 10, 2026 (17 days).
